title: incrementingWait overflows initial + increment*(n-1) for huge increments; overflow is clamped to 0, so Retryer sleeps 1000, 0, 998, 0, ... ms
cause: IncrementingWaitStrategy.computeSleepTime computes initialSleepTime + increment * (attemptNumber - 1) in unchecked long arithmetic and maps any negative (overflowed) result to 0 (WaitStrategies.java:282-283). Neither the incrementingWait factory nor the constructor bounds increment (only initialSleepTime >= 0 is checked), and TimeUnit.toMillis saturates large increments to Long.MAX_VALUE.
trigger: Public API only: RetryerBuilder.withWaitStrategy(WaitStrategies.incrementingWait(1000, MILLISECONDS, Long.MAX_VALUE, MILLISECONDS)) or incrementingWait(1, SECONDS, Long.MAX_VALUE, DAYS), a stop strategy that allows at least 3 attempts (e.g. stopAfterAttempt(6)), and a callable whose attempts keep being rejected.
consequence: Retryer.call (Retryer.java:176-178) receives sleeps 1000, 0, 998, 0, 996 ms and Thread.sleep(0) re-invokes the user callable immediately after every even-numbered attempt, instead of the documented non-decreasing ('incrementing') waits (exact value exceeds Long.MAX_VALUE, i.e. effectively unbounded). For later attempts the sequence degenerates further (attempt 1002 returns Long.MAX_VALUE for initial 1000, then 0 again).
premises: incrementingWait/IncrementingWaitStrategy accept any increment unvalidated (only initialSleepTime >= 0 is checked) and TimeUnit.toMillis saturates oversized increments to Long.MAX_VALUE.

Retryer.call passes computeSleepTime's value straight to BlockStrategy.block with no downstream correction; the default ThreadSleepStrategy calls Thread.sleep(sleepTime), so 0 means an immediate retry.

The trigger needs an extreme increment (at least about Long.MAX_VALUE/(n-1) ms to overflow within n attempts), e.g. a Long.MAX_VALUE sentinel or a saturating TimeUnit conversion; moderate increments cannot overflow before the int attempt counter reaches ~2^31.
The factory Javadoc promises 'incrementing amounts of time after each additional failed attempt'; the sibling Fibonacci/Exponential strategies saturate on overflow instead of collapsing to 0.
